# Jubilees Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Prologue — Revelation to Moses on Sinai

---

**1:1** And-it-came-to-pass in the first year of the going-out of the children-of-Israel from-the-land-of Egypt, in the third month, on the sixteenth day of the month, that God spoke to Moses, saying: "Come-up to me on the mountain, and I will give to-you two tablets of-stone of-the-law and of-the-commandment which I have written, that you may instruct them."

**1:2** And Moses went-up to the mountain of God. And the glory of the LORD settled upon Mount Sinai, and a cloud overshadowed it six days.

**1:3** And he called to Moses on the seventh day out-of-the-midst of the cloud, and the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a flaming fire on the top of the mountain.

**1:4** And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and God taught him the earlier-history and the later-history of the division of all the days of the law and of the testimony.

**1:5** And he said: "Set your heart upon all the words which I shall speak to you on this day, and write them in a book, that their generations may see how I have not forsaken them in-all the evil which they have wrought in transgressing the covenant which I establish between me and you this day on Mount Sinai."

**1:6** "And thus shall it be: when all these things come upon them, they will recognize that I am more-righteous than they in all their judgments and in all their deeds, and they will recognize that I have truly been with them."

**1:7** "And you, write for yourself all these words which I declare to you on this day, for I know their rebellion and their stiff-neck, before I bring them into the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying: 'To your seed I will give a land flowing with-milk and with-honey.'"

**1:8** "And they shall eat and be-satisfied, and they will turn to strange gods — to those which cannot deliver them from any of their afflictions — and this testimony shall serve as a witness against them."

**1:9** "For they will forget all my commandments, even-all which I command them, and they will walk after the gentiles and after their uncleanness and after their shame, and they will serve their gods, and these shall become to them a stumbling-block and an affliction and a torment and a snare."

**1:10** "And many will perish and they will be seized and fall into the hand of the enemy, because they have forsaken my statutes and my commandments and the festivals of my covenant and my sabbaths and my holy-things which I have hallowed in their-midst, and my tabernacle and my sanctuary which I have sanctified in their midst, and my name which dwells upon them."

**1:11** "And they will make for themselves high-places and sacred-pillars and graven-images, and they will bow-down to the works-of their own hands — each one to his idol — and these will be to them a stumbling-block."

**1:12** "And I will send witnesses to them that I may witness against them, but they will not hear, and they will slay the witnesses also, and they will persecute those who seek the law, and they will abolish and change everything, working evil before my eyes."

**1:13** "And I will hide my face from them, and I will deliver them into the hand of the gentiles for captivity and for a prey and for devouring, and I will remove them from the midst of the land, and I will scatter them among all the gentiles."

**1:14** "And they will forget all my law and all my commandments and all my judgments, and they will err regarding the new-moons and the sabbaths and the festivals and the jubilees and the ordinances."

**1:15** "And after this they will return to me from among the gentiles with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their strength, and I will gather them from among all the gentiles, and they will seek me, and I will be-found by them when they seek me with all their heart and with all their soul."

**1:16** "And I will disclose to them great peace, and I will build them as a plant-of righteousness with all my heart and with all my soul, and they shall be for a blessing and not for a curse, and they shall be the head and not the tail."

**1:17** "And I will build my sanctuary in their midst, and I will dwell with them, and I will be their God and they shall be my true and righteous people."

**1:18** "And I will not forsake them and I will not be estranged from them, for I am the LORD their God."

**1:19** And Moses fell upon his face and prayed and said: "O LORD my God, do not forsake your people and your inheritance, so that they should wander in the error of their hearts, and do not deliver them into the hand of their enemies the gentiles, lest they rule over them and cause them to sin against you."

**1:20** "Let your mercy, O LORD, be lifted-up upon your people, and create for them an upright spirit, and let not the spirit-of Beliar rule over them to accuse them before you and to ensnare them from every path of righteousness, so that they may perish from before your face."

**1:21** "But they are your people and your inheritance, whom you have delivered with your great power from the hand of the Egyptians. Create for them a clean heart and a holy spirit, and let them not be ensnared in their sins henceforth and forever."

**1:22** And the LORD said to Moses: "I know their contrariness and their thoughts and their stiff-neckedness, and they will not be obedient until they acknowledge their own sin and the sins of their fathers."

**1:23** "And after this they will return to me in all uprightness and with all their heart and with all their soul, and I will circumcise the foreskin-of their heart and the foreskin-of the heart of their seed, and I will create in them a holy spirit, and I will cleanse them so that they shall not turn away from me from that day and forever."

**1:24** "And their souls will cleave to me and to all my commandments, and they will fulfill my commandments, and I will be their Father and they shall be my children."

**1:25** "And they all shall be called children-of the living God, and every angel and every spirit shall know — yea, they shall know — that these are my children, and that I am their Father in uprightness and in righteousness, and that I love them."

**1:26** "And do-you write for Moses all the words which I tell to-you: the first-things and the last-things, which shall come to pass in all the divisions of the days in the law and in the testimony and in the weeks and the jubilees, until I descend and dwell with them throughout-all eternity."

**1:27** And he said to the angel-of-the-presence: "Write for Moses from the beginning of creation until my sanctuary shall be built among them for all eternity."

**1:28** "And the LORD will appear to the eyes of all, and all shall know that I am the God of Israel and the Father of all the children of Jacob and King upon Mount Zion for all eternity. And Zion and Jerusalem shall be holy."

**1:29** And the angel-of-the-presence, who went before the camp of Israel, took the tablets of the divisions of the years from the time of the creation of the law and of the testimony for the weeks of the jubilees, according to the individual years, according to all the number of the jubilees, and he related to Moses the divisions of all the days of the law and of the testimony until he had finished speaking.

---
*EMET notes: Ge'ez construct-chains rendered with hyphens. "Angel-of-the-presence" (mal'ak ze-yeqawwem westa 'egziabher) preserved as title. "Beliar" (v.20) = Ge'ez Beliar, the adversarial spirit. "Plant of righteousness" (v.16) is a Jubilees/Enochic technical term.*
